result.summary:
FULL SUITE RUN, foreground/blocking/synchronous (bash scripts/test_parallel.sh, TEST_PARALLEL_N derived from nproc=16, not overridden). Postgres already running and healthy (letflow-2-postgres-1, port 5472 per this workspace's own .env LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5472) -- no docker compose up needed or run. Started 2026-09-04T02:44:35Z, combined result ready ~7.5 minutes later.

COMBINED TALLY (real, quoted from the script's own aggregation, not estimated): 'combined: 3184 tests, 6 properties, 1 failures (3189/3190 passed)'. Per-partition: 16 partitions, 15 clean (0 failures each), partition 3 alone reported '188 tests, 0 properties, 1 failures, exit 2'. Script's own real exit code is 1 (test_parallel.sh:372 `exit "$any_failed"`) -- note an earlier 'EXIT_CODE:0' I captured during the interactive run reflected the shell pipe's (tee's) exit status, not the script's; corrected explicitly in the written report rather than left standing.

BASELINE COMPARISON: pre-change baseline 3192 tests; branch adds exactly one new test so expected 3193. TEST-DESIGNER and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR both measured 3193 passed on their own full runs during Step 4. This run's total collected (3184 tests + 6 properties = 3190) does not line up 1:1 with the prior 3193 figure -- most plausibly a counting-methodology difference between scripts/test_parallel.sh's per-partition exclusion accounting and mix letflow.check.test's single-process tally (not reconciled line-by-line here, since it is not the actionable finding). THE ACTIONABLE FINDING IS THE 1 REAL FAILURE, confirmed deterministic, not an aggregate-count artifact.

FAILURE: 'test ISS-0440 -- run/1 end-to-end via --dir, isolated tmp fixtures T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS -- default no-flag invocation still scans @handoffs_dir (Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest)' at test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:686. Raw output: '** (Mix.Error) letflow.lint_handoffs found 2 new violation(s) -- see output above', code `io = capture_io(fn -> assert LintHandoffs.run([]) == :ok end)`, stacktrace through Mix.raise/2 and ExUnit.CaptureIO -- i.e. the test's own capture_io assertion raised because the real-corpus scan under test found violations, not because of any assertion mismatch in the test body itself.

ISOLATED REPRODUCTION (confirms deterministic, not flaky): re-ran `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` alone afterward -- 'Result: 42/43 passed, Failed: 1 test', the SAME test, every time. This does not match either of this suite's documented flake classes (ISS-0352 wasm_hang / isolation-subprocess; ISS-0426 :lua_wallclock_race / wall-clock) by name, tag, or mechanism -- it reproduces because the test scans the real, static handoffs/ directory by design (its own name says so), and that directory's content is deterministic within a checkout, not timing-dependent.

ROOT CAUSE, read directly from `mix letflow.lint_handoffs`'s own output: exactly 2 new (un-grandfathered) hard violations, both [H3] 'non-schema top-level key(s): ["note"]', in handoffs/WF03-ISS0446-20260904/step-04b-test-design-validator-regate.json and .../step-04b-test-design-validator-regate2.json. Confirmed by reading both files directly: each carries a top-level `"note": "..."` field that is not among lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex's @schema_top_keys (handoff_id, run_id, workflow_id, step, from_agent, to_agent, file, created_at, started_at, completed_at, status, priority, context, task, result, rework_count, max_rework, not_agent_attested, gate_history -- 'note' absent). lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex itself is byte-identical to main (`git diff main...HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` empty) -- the lint tool did not change; the corpus it scans did, correctly triggering it.

ATTRIBUTION: STRUCTURAL and CAUSAL, not merely proximate. Both violating files are on this branch's own diff (`git log --oneline` on each shows exactly one commit each, both on this branch: 5abfc320 and ee2dc2ee, both TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate commits from this same run). The failing test's entire purpose is to assert a default lint_handoffs run over the REAL corpus returns :ok; the corpus now genuinely contains 2 files this branch added with a genuine, correctly-detected schema violation that did not exist before this branch. This is NOT the ISS-0446 fix itself: test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs (the actual scoped change) had no failures reported anywhere in this run's 16 partitions, consistent with every prior step's clean runs (ELIXIR-DEV 42 passed; TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR rework2/regate2, 43 passed repeatedly). This is a handoff-schema hygiene defect TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR introduced into its own gate artefacts at steps 04b and 04b-regate2.

OWNERSHIP: handoffs/ and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex are outside TEST-RUNNER's owned surface (test/letflow/process_instance_test.exs, other test files, test/support/data_case.ex). Per 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' this was reported, not silently patched. No code or handoff files were edited this step; git status --porcelain confirmed empty at start and this step made no changes other than the report/handoff files themselves.

SCOPE REMINDER, as instructed: this run verifies 'does this branch break anything' for pre-merge purposes -- it is NOT and is not being reported as evidence the ISS-0446 race is fixed (structural argument, already settled at design/review gates; a green teardown-race test proves nothing about the race either way, per the issue's own note that the failing CI run also passed 3192/3192 locally).
